articles.title: Haridwar activists flag ‘poor planning’ in Rs 21-crore road project
articles.summary: Haridwar activists allege poor planning in Rs 21-crore Kumbh-funded road project, citing narrowed roads, congestion, drainage issues and construction quality concerns.
articles.body: Haridwar: Social activists in Haridwar have raised concerns over a Rs 21-crore road and footpath upgrade project, alleging that “poor planning has narrowed roads and worsened traffic congestion in several areas.”The project, funded through Kumbh Mela budget, involves the construction of footpaths on both sides of major roads across Haridwar, including Kankhal, Shankar Ashram, Bhagat Singh Chowk and Hill Bypass Road.Activists said footpaths have been built without clearing existing encroachments, while electricity poles and trees remained in place. They also alleged that the work has done little to improve the drainage system.Social activist J P Badoni told TOI that the new footpaths had reduced the usable width of key roads, leaving little space for parking and causing traffic bottlenecks. “There is an acute lack of planning in the development of footpaths and road-widening projects,” Badoni said. He also warned that the lack of proper drainage along Hill Bypass Road could cause severe waterlogging during the monsoon.Residents have also questioned the quality of construction and called for an inquiry into the use of funds. Local resident R M Dobhal said the quality of work was being compromised at several sites, despite the appointment of a third-party agency to monitor the project. “The Mela administration should take the matter seriously and stern action should be taken against the responsible officials,” he said.Kumbh Mela administration, however, said the upgrades were necessary to manage the large crowds expected during the festival.Additional mela officer Dayanand Saraswati told TOI that footpaths were essential for the city ahead of Kumbh Mela. He said authorities were taking action against encroachments and regularly inspecting the work. “No compromise will be made on the quality of the works,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.summary: An elderly woman’s wishes were nearly derailed into a family-wide legal dispute due to one additional document that was part of a carefully planned
articles.body: An elderly woman’s wishes were nearly derailed into a family-wide legal dispute due to one additional document that was part of a carefully planned inheritance. A simple plan to split a £1million fortune equally between two close relatives escalated into a long court battle after a seemingly ordinary clause in a second will put 16 distant family members in line for a share. The question of who will inherit has finally been settled by a London High Court ruling, almost three years after the dispute began.According to reports by The Independent and The Express Gazette, the court ruled that Dorothy Eirwen George’s 2017 English will was valid, meaning her niece and nephew will inherit her estate, rather than it being split amongst her wider family.Two wills, one inheritance planGeorge, a retired teacher from Bexleyheath in south London, passed away in December 2023, aged 83, leaving an estate worth an estimated £1 million. Her assets included property and other holdings in the UK and a holiday apartment near Limassol in Cyprus.According to The Independent, in May 2017 she wrote an English will naming her niece, Helen Thyer, and nephew, Peter Crawford, as beneficiaries of her UK estate. Four months later she made a second will in Cyprus, leaving her holiday apartment to Thyer only.The arrangement was meant to make sure both relatives got inheritances of equal value, reports The Independent. Crawford was given the English document so that he could receive a corresponding cash legacy, while the Cypriot will gave the overseas property to Thyer.However, the second document contained a general revocation clause that seemed to invalidate all previous wills, making it unclear whether George’s original instructions for inheritance remained legally valid, the report adds.Broader family claims faced legal complicationsAfter George's death Thyer and Crawford realized that the wording of the Cyprus will might invalidate the English document. If this was the case, then their aunt would have died intestate in relation to her UK estate, which means her assets would be divided in accordance with inheritance law, and not her expressed wishes, explains another report by The Express Gazette.This would have added sixteen more relatives to the inheritance, bringing the total number of beneficiaries to eighteen. The siblings, 73 and 71 years old, then hired professional genealogists to find distant relatives whose whereabouts they did not know fully. Those identified were seen as possible beneficiaries if the original English will was not recognized,the online report adds.The siblings insisted their aunt did not intend the second document to supersede her earlier arrangements, the Express Gazette said.High Court considers woman's motivesThe siblings took the dispute to London’s High Court, arguing that the revocation clause had been included by mistake and that the will for Cyprus was only meant to cover the holiday property.Their barrister Michael O’Sullivan testified that George had always planned to leave her English estate to both relatives. A witness statement in support of the claim was also given by her friend Rosemary Sanger, who said George had spoken of her plans to divide the UK assets between the siblings, leaving the Cyprus apartment to Thyer, adds The Independent.Master Katherine McQuail looked at the evidence and found that the existence of a revocation clause in a later will does not automatically invalidate an earlier document where the deceased had no intention of canceling it.George had intended the Cyprus will to include her overseas property and had not tried to revoke the English document, drawn up just four months before, the judge said.Siblings get £1 million inheritanceIn the end, the High Court upheld the May 2017 English will, safeguarding the siblings’ right to inherit their aunt’s estate. The judge also noted that none of the other 16 possible further beneficiaries had come forward to dispute the claim.The court also ordered that George's estate pay out more than £35,000 spent by the siblings pursuing the case.The Independent and The Express Gazette said the long-running dispute had gone on for almost three years and had been a huge financial and emotional strain.The result also underlined the importance of careful drafting of multiple wills – in particular where assets are held in different countries. One clause in the following document had almost managed to achieve the opposite of what George had intended as a fair inheritance arrangement.Images Courtesy: Champion News and Google GeminiYou use AI every day. articles.body: Friendships may move more slowly than Gemini would like this Thursday. This morning, the Moon in your own sign forms a sextile with Jupiter in Leo, your third house of neighbours, peers, and everyday connections. The angle brings warmth and a wish to reach out. Yet replies may come late, plans may shift, and some friends may seem busier than usual during wedding season. Shani, retrograde in Pisces, your tenth house, teaches patience. Strong social bonds don't depend on constant contact, and reading too much into silence can create problems that don't exist.When Friends Seem DistantWith the Moon in Gemini, your feelings are close to the surface. A missed call, a one-word reply, or a gathering you weren't invited to may sting more than it should. Mars, ruler of your eleventh house of friends and social circles, sits in Leo beside Jupiter and Ketu. Ketu can make people seem distracted or withdrawn without any real reason linked to you.Give others the same understanding you would want when your own week is busy.Shani’s Lesson in Steady FriendshipShani in your tenth house links your social life with responsibility and reputation. It values loyalty over frequency. Friends who are steady over years matter more than those who are always available. If a friend is slow to respond, wait before assuming anything. If you feel left out of a group, consider whether it is a passing gap or a pattern worth discussing calmly.Jupiter Offers a Wider ViewJupiter’s sextile with the Moon in the morning brings perspective. A short, warm message to a friend without expecting a reply often strengthens a bond more than demanding attention. Today is Thursday, Jupiter’s own day, which supports generosity in how you see others.Creative Joy Is Close at HandMercury, your ruling planet, and Venus sit together in Libra, your fifth house of joy and creativity. Spending some time on a hobby or with family can ease any feeling of social disappointment. The Sun in Scorpio, your sixth house, keeps your daily routine steady.What to Do TodaySend a warm message to a friend without expecting an immediate reply. Don't assume a slow reply or a cancelled plan means anything. Raise any repeated pattern calmly rather than in frustration. Spend time on a hobby or with family if you feel lonely. Value long-standing friends over constant social activity.Shani Remedy for TodayChant “Om Mitraya Namah,” honouring the Sun as the friend of all beings, 108 times this Thursday. articles.title: After 30 years in jail, former Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassin seeks parity with Rajiv Gandhi's killer in SC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Invoking the ground of parity with former PM Rajiv Gandhi killer AG Perarivalan, who was a death convict but was allowed to be released and is
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Invoking the ground of parity with former PM Rajiv Gandhi killer AG Perarivalan, who was a death convict but was allowed to be released and is now a practising lawyer, Balwant Singh Rajoana, who has been in jail for over 30 years and is facing a death sentence for the assassination of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, requested the SC on Wednesday that the same reformative approach should be taken for him also and his sentence be commuted to life imprisonment. SC reserved its order.Appearing before a bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Singh, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, for Rajoana, said that he was a misguided youth at the time of the offence and he is now a reformed man. Rohatgi contended that Rajiv Gandhi killer Perarivalan is now a practising lawyer after his death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment and the sentence was later remitted by the apex court on the ground that he spent 30 years in jail. The senior advocate said his client also spent more than 30 years in jail and he should also be allowed the same relief.Opposing his plea, ASG KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, said that no relief should be extended to him as the convict had himself declared he did not have faith in the Constitution and judicial system. But Rohatgi said the statement was made 30 years ago during trial and that should not be a ground to deny him liberty after three decades.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
